findings.detail: The token-split defect recorded in the Nit round still occurs when the preceding command contains quoted hash text. Two physical lines containing `some-command "literal # data" 2\` and `>/dev/null` form an unreasoned stderr discard in Bash, but both pass the guard. The hash heuristic prevents the corrected continuation join from applying. This belongs to the branch-introduced guard and retains the prior Important severity. The recurring grammar defect calls for structural tokenization or an explicitly supported grammar that rejects unsupported forms, rather than another regex exception.
findings.evidence: At line 74, the space before the quoted hash makes line_continues return 0. Lines 155-160 therefore check and clear the first fragment without joining it. Neither that fragment nor the remaining `>/dev/null` matches check_output. The installed Bash manual's QUOTING section confirms that the quoted hash is literal and the unquoted backslash-newline is removed. The split-discard-token fixture covers the split without quoted hash text; allowed-hash-text does not split a redirect token. The prior batch-1 report and commit d7bf9812 establish the earlier finding and attempted fix.
findings.title: Sibling input forms: replace grouping that still misses split redirects

findings.detail: A script containing `some-command 2>&-` passes without an exception while closing stderr, so child diagnostics cannot reach the caller. The sibling spelling `2<&-` also closes descriptor 2 and passes. These should require the same reason as other intentional suppression. This is a gap in the branch-introduced discard guard, present since its initial implementation.
findings.evidence: shorthand_kind excludes >& preceded by a digit. The discard expression recognizes file redirects only, while the capture expression recognizes duplication to descriptor 1 or a file destination; neither recognizes descriptor closure. The installed Bash manual's Duplicating File Descriptors section specifies that word '-' closes descriptor n, for both input and output duplication. The live-descriptor control exercises >&2, not closing stderr.
findings.title: Sibling input forms: closing stderr bypasses the discard rule

findings.detail: An unavailable upstream lookup still becomes a successful empty result. If the other lookups produce no drift rows, the script exits successfully with empty stdout, and the repository workflow closes an existing drift issue despite the incomplete audit. Keeping stderr live exposes the error but does not prevent the incorrect action. This predates the supplied base; it is the repository-tooling sibling of the Important version-audit finding already recorded in batch 4 and deferred in the ledger.
findings.evidence: The Node lookup at lines 66-70 converts failure to an empty latest value and returns successfully. Other lookup helpers repeat this handling. print_report emits nothing when drift_rows is empty. .github/workflows/version-audit.yml sets has_drift=false for that empty stdout and closes the existing issue at lines 82-89. The base commit contains the same failure-to-empty behavior.
findings.title: Absent or partial data: upstream failures still become a no-drift success
